title: User Account Control is enabled
description: User Account Control mediates elevation to administrative rights. With it off, any process started by a member of the local Administrators group runs fully elevated with no prompt and no split token.
rationale: Disabling UAC removes the boundary that stops a single user-context compromise becoming immediate administrative control of the machine.
remediation: Set EnableLUA to 1 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System and restart the host.

title: Windows Firewall service is running
description: The Windows Defender Firewall service enforces host packet filtering.
rationale: With the service stopped, every profile's rules are inert and the host accepts whatever the network offers it.
remediation: Start-Service MpsSvc and set its start type to Automatic.

title: Telnet server is not installed
description: The Telnet server service, which carries credentials in clear text.
rationale: Telnet authenticates over an unencrypted channel; anyone able to observe the path recovers the password.
remediation: Uninstall the Telnet Server feature and use SSH or WinRM over HTTPS instead.

title: Minimum password length is at least 14 characters
description: The local security policy's minimum password length.
rationale: Length is the property that most directly resists offline cracking of a recovered hash.
remediation: Set Minimum password length to 14 or more in the local security policy, or through the domain password policy where the host is joined.

title: SSH does not permit password-based root login
description: Whether the SSH daemon accepts a direct root login with a password.
rationale: Direct root login removes the accountability of a named account and gives a single guessed password full control of the host.
remediation: Set 'PermitRootLogin prohibit-password' (or 'no') in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and reload sshd.

title: /etc/passwd is not group- or world-writable
description: Filesystem mode of the local account database.
rationale: A writable /etc/passwd allows an unprivileged user to add an account, or to blank the password field of an existing one.
remediation: chmod 0644 /etc/passwd && chown root:root /etc/passwd

title: The audit daemon is running
description: auditd records kernel audit events to disk.
rationale: Without it there is no local record of privilege use or of changes to the files these other rules check, so an incident cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
remediation: Install and enable auditd, then define an audit ruleset.

title: No telnet daemon is listening
description: TCP 23, the telnet service port.
rationale: Telnet transmits credentials and session content in clear text on a network where anyone on the path can read them.
remediation: Remove the telnet server package and use SSH.

title: Password maximum age is set
description: PASS_MAX_DAYS from /etc/login.defs.
rationale: An unbounded password lifetime means a credential compromised years ago is still valid today.
remediation: Set PASS_MAX_DAYS in /etc/login.defs and apply with chage.

title: /etc/crontab is not writable by unprivileged users
description: Filesystem mode of the system crontab.
rationale: A writable system crontab is a direct path to code execution as root at the next scheduled run.
remediation: chmod 0644 /etc/crontab && chown root:root /etc/crontab

title: No service grants configuration rights to a non-administrator
description: Every service's security descriptor is read and checked for an access-control entry granting a non-administrative principal the right to change the service's configuration.
rationale: A principal that can change a service's configuration can point its binary path at anything and restart it. That is SYSTEM on the next start, with no further condition — the shortest path from an ordinary account to full control of the host.
remediation: Remove CHANGE_CONFIG, WRITE_DAC, WRITE_OWNER and ALL_ACCESS from non-administrative principals on the named services: sc.exe sdset <service> <SDDL>. Only Administrators and SYSTEM should hold them.

title: No directory on root's PATH is writable by a non-root user
description: Each directory on root's PATH is checked for group- or world-writability, and for direct writability by the scanning account.
rationale: Anything root runs by name resolves through PATH. A writable directory on it lets an unprivileged user place a binary that root then executes — an unconditional path to root that needs no other weakness.
remediation: chmod go-w on the named directories, or remove them from root's PATH. A directory that must be writable does not belong on it.

title: No PostgreSQL login role has an empty password
description: Login roles whose password is unset. Such a role authenticates against any pg_hba rule that does not itself demand a password.
rationale: A login role with no password is usable by anyone who can reach the port under a 'trust' rule, and cannot be used at all under a password rule — so it is either an open door or a broken account, and both warrant attention.
remediation: ALTER ROLE <name> WITH PASSWORD '<value>'; for a role that should not log in, ALTER ROLE <name> WITH NOLOGIN.
expected: no login role without a password

title: PostgreSQL stores passwords with SCRAM rather than MD5
description: The algorithm new and changed passwords are stored under.
rationale: MD5 password verifiers are unsalted against the username only and are replayable: the stored hash is password-equivalent, so a read of pg_authid is enough to authenticate as the role.
remediation: Set password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256', reload, then reset each role's password so the stored verifier is re-derived — changing the setting alone does not re-encode existing passwords.

title: nginx does not advertise its version
description: Whether nginx includes its version in error pages and the Server header. Unset, nginx defaults to 'on'.
rationale: The exact patch version tells an attacker which published vulnerabilities apply before they probe for any of them, turning a scan of the estate into a target list.
remediation: Set 'server_tokens off;' in the http block and reload.

title: nginx does not expose the stub_status endpoint
description: Locations serving the stub_status module, which reports active connections and request counters.
rationale: stub_status is unauthenticated by default and discloses live traffic volumes and connection state — useful for timing an attack and for confirming that one is working.
remediation: Remove the stub_status location, or restrict it with 'allow'/'deny' to the monitoring host only.

title: Tomcat does not deploy the manager application
description: Whether Tomcat's bundled 'manager' application is deployed. The official image moves the bundled applications to webapps.dist/, so a stock container has none of them deployed.
rationale: The manager application deploys and undeploys web applications. An authenticated session with it is remote code execution by design, which is why it is the first thing every Tomcat credential-guessing tool tries.
remediation: Delete /usr/local/tomcat/webapps/manager if the application is not required. Where it is, restrict it by address and authenticate it against the organisation's directory.

title: No container runs with --privileged
description: Running containers started with --privileged, which disables essentially every isolation the runtime provides.
rationale: A privileged container gets all capabilities, unrestricted device access and no seccomp or AppArmor confinement. Escaping it to the host is not an exploit, it is a documented feature — mounting the host disk and chrooting into it takes two commands.
remediation: Remove --privileged and grant only the specific capabilities or device the workload needs, with --cap-add and --device.

title: The kubelet refuses anonymous requests
description: Whether the kubelet accepts unauthenticated requests to its API. Unset, the kubelet's own default is true; kubeadm writes false.
rationale: The kubelet API can list pods, read their logs and — with authorization also permissive — exec into containers. Anonymous access to it is unauthenticated access to every workload on the node.
remediation: Set authentication.anonymous.enabled: false in the kubelet configuration and restart the kubelet.

title: containerd verifies TLS for every registry mirror
description: Registries with a per-registry TLS configuration block. Such a block is where insecure_skip_verify is set, and its absence means containerd verifies every mirror normally.
rationale: A registry configured with insecure_skip_verify accepts any certificate, so an image pulled from it can be replaced in transit — and containerd runs whatever it receives as the container's contents.
remediation: Remove the per-registry TLS override and give the registry a certificate the host trusts. Where a private CA is used, add it to the host trust store rather than disabling verification.
